notes:
User wants high-quality, durable sandals with sturdy straps and plans to check Teva, Birkenstock, Sanuk, Merrell, and Keen at REI, DSW, Zappos, or Amazon. They want to organize their closet this weekend and are considering a shoe rack for old sneakers, which currently take up space. They may also inventory/declutter footwear, group by type, use dividers or stackable racks, and donate, sell, repair, recycle, or repurpose unused pairs.

Sneaker care/storage: User plans to have old sneakers polished and conditioned by a cobbler and will find one through friends, family, Google/Yelp reviews, professional membership, or a reputable mail-in service. Before storage, clean sneakers, ensure they are fully dry, use shoe trees/acid-free stuffing to hold shape, and use breathable shoe bags or dust-protective boxes. Store in a clean, ventilated, dry area away from sunlight and heat; use silica gel or odor absorbers, especially in humid conditions, and check periodically for moisture, mold, or mildew. Avoid stacking or compressing them.

User plans to donate old dress shoes to a local charity thrift store this Saturday. They will call ahead and check the website for guidelines. Shoes are somewhat worn but believed to be in acceptable condition; clean and polish them first and ensure no broken heels, torn seams, cracks, severe sole wear, or other damage.

User jogs regularly but has used the same route for months and wants a more scenic change. Their location is unknown. They can discover routes through Google Maps, local Parks and Recreation, Strava, MapMyRun, or Runkeeper, or ask local friends/joggers. For safety, consider daylight/reflective gear, traffic and pedestrian awareness, hydration, and sharing the route and return time.
